newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat says Saddam involved in Arab summit effort.
newsitem.headline: Arafat says Saddam involved in Arab summit effort.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Saturday Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein was involved in efforts to convene an emergency Arab summit to discuss the Israel-PLO peacemaking crisis.

"Saddam, (Abu Dhabi ruler) Sheikh Zaid (bin Sultan al-Nahayan) and myself are seeking to hold an emergency Arab summit to discuss the latest developments," Arafat said in a speech to the Palestinian legislature.
"We hope we will succeed in convening the summit as soon as possible," he said.
Such a diplomatic initiative would be the Iraqi president's first step into the Israeli-Arab arena since the 1991 Gulf war, when he launched Scud missile attacks against the Jewish state.
Last month Saddam made a speech in which he indirectly approved of the Israeli-PLO interim peace deals and called for holding an Arab summit on the Middle East peace process.
Israeli-Palestinian relations have plunged deeper into crisis since two Islamic suicide bombers killed 13 people in a Jerusalem market on July 30.
